summary: Shanghai's party chief is placed under investigation, Beijing extends a pause on a minerals ban, the first foreign astronaut reaches China's space station, and AI labs feel US chip limits.
body: Chen Jining, the Communist Party chief of Shanghai and a member of its Politburo, the party's top leadership group of about two dozen people, has been placed under investigation for "serious violations of discipline and law", usually a phrase for corruption.[^1][^2] He is the fourth member of the current Politburo investigated since 2025, and no successor has been named.[^1][^3] Chen, 62, is a former Tsinghua University president, environment minister and Beijing mayor. An analyst told AP that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign "has no limits"; another linked the timing to jockeying before the 2027 party congress, where Xi is expected to seek a fourth term.[^2][^1]

On trade, China kept its ban on exporting gallium, germanium and antimony to the US suspended until Jan. 27, Bloomberg reports.[^4] These metals go into chips, solar panels and military gear, and China produces most of the world's supply of gallium.[^4] The pause keeps the US-China trade truce alive after the Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen, even as Beijing protests new US limits on Chinese access to AI chips abroad, which Reuters sources say are delaying releases at labs such as Zhipu and Moonshot (see World).[^4][^5]

In space, Shenzhou-24 docked at China's Tiangong station on Wednesday carrying Zeeshan Ali, the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreigner aboard. He trained for seven months in Beijing, including lessons in Chinese and calligraphy, and will stay five to ten days.[^6] China still aims to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030.[^6]
differences: Beijing presents the Chen probe as anti-corruption work; outside analysts read it as part of a political contest before 2027.[^1][^2]
